requirement: Run an external command with subprocess.run, returning its stdout and turning timeouts, non-zero exits and signal deaths into typed exceptions that keep a bounded tail of stderr.
skeleton: CommandError and CommandTimeoutError exception classes, a stderr tail limit, and run_command validating argv, calling subprocess.run with a timeout, and mapping the outcomes.
caption: Running a command with subprocess.run and typed failures. run_command(argv, *, timeout=30.0) raises ValueError saying argv must not be empty, then runs list(argv) with capture_output, text mode, the timeout and check=False, and returns stdout. subprocess.TimeoutExpired becomes CommandTimeoutError, which stores the timeout and reads argv[0] timed out after timeout seconds. Any returncode other than 0, including negative codes from death by signal, raises CommandError holding the returncode and only the last STDERR_TAIL_CHARS, 500, characters of stderr, formatted as argv[0] exited with the code and that tail. The fixture asserts, running sys.executable -c scripts, that print output comes back, that exit 3 with 600 stderr characters keeps the final 500 b characters, that a process killing itself with SIGTERM raises CommandError with a negative code, that a sleep with timeout 0.5 raises CommandTimeoutError quickly, and that empty argv raises ValueError with the default timeout 30.

plan.intent: Call CLI tools from Python with failures callers can act on
constraints: The default timeout is 30 seconds and TimeoutExpired becomes CommandTimeoutError
Any non-zero returncode, including negative signal codes, raises CommandError
CommandError keeps the last 500 characters of stderr

rationale.teaches: Always pass a timeout to subprocess.run, check every non-zero returncode, and keep the end of stderr where the real error usually is.
rationale.why: No timeout hangs callers forever, checking only positive codes misses killed processes, and keeping the head of stderr drops the final error line.

ops.docstring: Run a command with a timeout and typed failures.

ops.source:
class CommandError(Exception):
    """The command exited with a non-zero status."""

    def __init__(self, argv: Sequence[str], returncode: int, stderr: str) -> None:
        tail = stderr[-STDERR_TAIL_CHARS:]
        super().__init__(f"{argv[0]} exited with {returncode}: {tail}")
        self.returncode = returncode
        self.stderr = tail

candidates.why_wrong: The first 500 stderr characters are kept, dropping the final error message.
A timeout escapes as the raw subprocess.TimeoutExpired instead of CommandTimeoutError.
Processes killed by a signal have negative codes and are treated as success.
Empty argv fails inside subprocess with an IndexError instead of ValueError.
Without an explicit timeout a hung command blocks forever.
